Olivia / team — I've reviewed the redline and flagged three DPA clauses where our standard positions diverge:

- Clause 5.2 (Subprocessor notification): MedIntel requests 30 days' notice + GC approval for new subprocessors. We can accept 30 days' notice but cannot require prior approval for all routine infra subprocessors; propose exception language for operational subprocessors with a right to object for "high-risk" categories.

- Clause 7.1 (Transfers & SCCs): the SCCs template provided has an extra obligation on processing location. We'll accept the SCCs but need to append a short transfer-impact addendum that describes residual risk and fallback routing (we'll provide suggested wording).

- Clause 9.4 (Audit windows): MedIntel's audit window request of on-demand audits is operationally heavy; propose a quarterly scheduled evidence package plus ad-hoc audit with reasonable notice.

I'll produce tracked-change text and a short rationale for each in the attached DPA_markups_v1.docx (will be uploaded to the shared Drive). For now, Hannah's technical annex will be the best place to capture the per-activity transfer paths.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: MedIntel DPA redline + technical annex questions

Olivia — attaching the first-draft technical annex below. High-level notes:

- Egress regions: primary processing occurs in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 (AWS). Secondary egress for batching/backups may transit us-east-1 for disaster recovery; long-term object storage replicas may be in eu-west-1 or us-east-1 depending on customer residency controls.
- Subprocessor activities that may involve cross-border transfer: monitoring/observability exports (aggregated logs), nightly backups for disaster-recovery, managed model hosting for dedicated customers where the control plane may be in a different jurisdiction.
- We include a short mitigation list: IP-restricted transfer channels, encrypted-at-rest snapshots, and the option to pin data replication to EU-only for dedicated contracts.

Action items for you: confirm if pinning EU-only replication is required for the SKU in question (MedIntel-Prod-Standard) or optional. If required, Ben will provide pricing delta and Marcus will add the field to the Order Form.

Attachment: Technical_Annex_MedIntel_v1.txt (plain text)

Hannah

Hannah / Laura / team — this is helpful, thanks. Two quick confirmations from our side:

1) Pin EU-only replication is required for the MedIntel-Prod-Standard SKU (we cannot accept cross-border replication for primary customer data). Please add the EU-only option as a checkbox in the Order Form with an associated price delta.
2) For subprocessors, the "high-risk" category is acceptable (we'll provide a short list of roles we consider high-risk: data-science access, long-term archival vendors, and live support engineers).

If you can send the updated Order Form row + tracked DPA language by EOD Friday, I'll escalate to our GC and procurement to keep the timeline intact.

Olivia
Head of Security & Privacy, MedIntel
